"Dream Lover" is a song written by American musician Bobby Darin; he recorded his composition on March 5, 1959, and released it as a single the following month.  It was produced by Ahmet Ertegun and Jerry Wexler and engineered by Tom Dowd. The song has been widely covered by other singers.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: In addition to Darin's vocal, the song features [[Neil Sedaka]] on piano.<ref>{{cite interview |interviewer=Russell A. Trunk |url=http://www.annecarlini.com/ex_interviews.php?id=710 |title=Neil Sedaka, Still Keeping It Together |work=Exclusive Magazine |access-date=April 7, 2008}}</ref>  While recording it, Darin decided to stretch out some [[chord changes]] he found on the piano and add strings and voices.<ref name=pc13>{{Pop Chronicles |13| 2|Bobby Darin}}</ref> A picture sleeve, featuring a portrait of Darin, was also issued for this record in the U.S.
sections.text: In addition to Darin's vocal, the song features Neil Sedaka on piano.  While recording it, Darin decided to stretch out some chord changes he found on the piano and add strings and voices. A picture sleeve, featuring a portrait of Darin, was also issued for this record in the U.S.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: It was released as a single on [[Atco Records]] in the U.S. in 1959, and became a multimillion seller, reaching number 2 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for a week,<ref name="BB61559">"[https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/50s/1959/Billboard%201959-06-08.pdf The Billboard Hot 100]", ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''. June 8, 1959. p. 38. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> number 4 on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'}}s [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|Hot R&B Sides]] chart,<ref>"[https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/50s/1959/Billboard%201959-06-15.pdf Hot R&B Sides]", ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''. June 15, 1959. p. 39. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> and number 5 in [[CHUM Chart|Canada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chumtribute.com/59-05-25-chart.jpg| title=CHUM Hit Parade - May 25, 1959}}</ref> "Dream Lover" was kept from the number-one spot by "[[The Battle of New Orleans]]" by [[Johnny Horton]].<ref name="BB61559"/> It did reach number 1, though, on the UK's ''[[New Musical Express]]'' chart for four weeks during July 1959.<ref>[https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/6337/bobby-darin/ Bobby Darin - Full Official Chart History], ''[[Official Charts Company]]''. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> The song also reached number 5 on Norway's [[VG-lista|''VG''-lista]],<ref>[https://norwegiancharts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Bobby+Darin&titel=Dream+Lover&cat=s Bobby Darin - Dream Lover], ''norwegiancharts.com''. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> number 12 in [[Flanders]], and number 21 in [[Wallonia]].<ref>[https://www.ultratop.be/nl/song/1b755/Bobby-Darin-Dream-Lover Bobby Darin - Dream Lover], ''[[Ultratop]]''. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref>
sections.text: It was released as a single on Atco Records in the U.S. in 1959, and became a multimillion seller, reaching number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 for a week, number 4 on Billboard{{'}}s Hot R&B Sides chart, and number 5 in Canada. "Dream Lover" was kept from the number-one spot by "The Battle of New Orleans" by Johnny Horton. It did reach number 1, though, on the UK's New Musical Express chart for four weeks during July 1959. The song also reached number 5 on Norway's VG-lista, number 12 in Flanders, and number 21 in Wallonia.

sections.heading: Certifications
Cover versions
sections.wikitext:
In 1971, [[Billy "Crash" Craddock]] released his version of "Dream Lover" as a single. Craddock's version reached number 1 on ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cash Box]]''{{'}}s Country Top 65 chart<ref>"[https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1971/Cash-Box-1971-09-04.pdf Cash Box Country Top 65]", ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cash Box]]''. September 4, 1971. p. 64. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> and ''[[Record World]]''{{'}}s Country Singles Chart,<ref>"[https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/71/Record-World-1971-08-28.pdf The Country Singles Chart]", ''[[Record World]]''. August 28, 1971. p. 45. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> while reaching number 5 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s [[Hot Country Songs|Hot Country Singles]] chart.<ref>"[https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/70s/1971/Billboard%201971-08-14.pdf Hot Country Singles]", ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''. August 14, 1971. p. 26. Retrieved February 5, 2021.</ref> Craddock's version was included on his 1972 album ''[[You Better Move On (album)|You Better Move On]]''.<ref>"[https://books.google.com/books?id=_ycEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA54 Billboard Album Reviews]", ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''. February 5, 1972. p. 54. Retrieved February 6, 2021.</ref>

In 1979, [[Ricky Nelson]] released a cover of "Dream Lover". His version reached number 29 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Adult Contemporary chart and number 59 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s [[Hot Country Songs|Hot Country Singles]] chart. He sang the song on his appearance on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''. Also in 1979, Australian [[Glen Shorrock]] of [[Little River Band]] covered it. It was in the Australian Top 10 for eighteen weeks that year.<ref>See here ({{ YouTube | SuWXTuXuCZA | Dream Lover, Glenn Shorrock }})</ref>

[[Tanya Tucker]] and [[Glen Campbell]] released a duet version in 1980 on the album ''[[Dreamlovers (album)|Dreamlovers]]''. Their version hit number 59 on the US country chart, and number 48 in Canada.
sections.text:
In 1971, Billy "Crash" Craddock released his version of "Dream Lover" as a single. Craddock's version reached number 1 on Cash Box{{'}}s Country Top 65 chart and Record World{{'}}s Country Singles Chart, while reaching number 5 on Billboard{{'}}s Hot Country Singles chart. Craddock's version was included on his 1972 album You Better Move On.

In 1979, Ricky Nelson released a cover of "Dream Lover". His version reached number 29 on Billboard{{'}}s Adult Contemporary chart and number 59 on Billboard{{'}}s Hot Country Singles chart. He sang the song on his appearance on Saturday Night Live. Also in 1979, Australian Glen Shorrock of Little River Band covered it. It was in the Australian Top 10 for eighteen weeks that year.

Tanya Tucker and Glen Campbell released a duet version in 1980 on the album Dreamlovers. Their version hit number 59 on the US country chart, and number 48 in Canada.
